summary_points: Document is for installation, start-up, operation, and maintenance of oil to salt heat exchangers.
Important notes include removing orange parts, checking plug tightness, notifying LOINTEK for warranty work, and being cautious when entering the system.
Table of contents includes sections on shipping/installation, start-up/operation, maintenance/reparations, and documentation.
Heaters must be plugged with a nitrogen nozzle and maintained at 0.1 bar pressure.
Installation requires true horizontal plane as per General Arrangement Drawing.
Two hook lift is for horizontal vessels only, avoiding strikes and bumps.
Slings should be nylon with rubber protection if using steel slings.
Proper rigging required for lifting Oil to Salt Heat Exchanger Systems.
Fixed supports need shims, foundation bolts must be loosened.
Anchor bolt stakeout must match equipment drill distribution.
All bolt elements must be correctly installed before lifting.
Pipelines should be blown before welding to equipment.
Corrosion protection with nitrogen; heater should remain sealed until piping is complete.
Any alterations or repairs must be made under LOINTEK direction and in accordance with LOINTEK procedures.
Initial start-up involves filling empty heat exchangers with preheated HTF and gradually increasing temperature.
Warm start-up requires following specific temperature and flow rate guidelines for normal charge or discharge.
Shutdown sequence should prioritize stopping hot fluid before cold side to prevent damage.
Drainage procedures include protecting against pressure differences and maintaining temperature limits.
Field welding must follow specific certification and procedure guidelines.
Shell removal requires careful handling to prevent bundle damage.
Reinstallation involves precise alignment and monitoring during insertion.
Radiographic examination is required for certain carbon steel seams.
Hydro test must be conducted after all connections are welded.
Bolted connections must be tightened uniformly in a diametrically staggered pattern.
Torque values for SA-193-B7 studs are provided in the document.
Gaskets should be inspected before installation and repaired if damaged.
Tube failures should be located by recording specific details about each failure.
Visual and penetrant tests can help detect damages in tubesheet weldings.
Safety plugs must be applied to tube-end peet joints before welding.
Avoid working around the area being welded until heat has subsided.
Base material must be clean for proper welding.
No holes should be adjacent to the weld area during plug welding.
Thoroughly test tubesheet plugs as per LOI-039-062-0004-GAR Rev.01 instructions.
Use caution when removing pass partition cover bolting to ensure secure removal.
Nuts holding the cover plate should be removed to remove the cover.
Remove the pass partition cover gasket before replacement.
Inspect and repair suspect areas before installing new gaskets.
Obtain new pass partition gaskets for proper sealing.
Hydrostatic test pressures must not be exceeded and should be verified on the nameplate.
Water temperature during hydrostatic testing should be at least 60 OF to avoid potential issues.
warnings: Do not attempt to remove covers or plugs from pressurized vessels.
Bleed nitrogen pressure down to zero before removing gasket cover bolts.
